domains.proposed_domain: Finite representation construction for operator algebra research

evidence.quote: Thus the projection $e$ lies in the reduced completion but not in the group ring.

exclusions.query: Nontrivial idempotents in the complex group ring of the constructed group
exclusions.reason: The projection lies in the reduced completion, while the paper explicitly states that the group ring has only trivial scalar idempotents.

evidence.quote: There exist a finitely generated torsion-free discrete group $G_{\mathrm{proj}}$ and a projection $e\in C_r^*(G_{\mathrm{proj}})$ such that $$0<\tau_{G_{\mathrm{proj}}}(e)<\frac12.$$

exclusions.query: Projectionlessness for every torsion-free group fails by the same construction
exclusions.reason: The paper constructs an existential counterexample and separately records substantial classes for which projectionlessness holds.

evidence.quote: In particular, the estimates below do not merely test some finite-dimensional representations of the deck group.

exclusions.query: Finite-dimensional spectral experiments certify the global reduced spectral band
exclusions.reason: The approximation is required in the full regular representation; testing selected finite-dimensional representations is insufficient.

evidence.quote: The comparison with the assigned domains proves spectral separation, but their ordering need not be equivariant.

exclusions.query: The well-order of assigned domains is equivariant
exclusions.reason: Domain disjointness supplies spectral comparison, but trace comparison is obtained from the separate equivariant all-copy restriction construction.

evidence.quote: The direct sum is algebraic, so every tuple used has finite support.

exclusions.query: An infinite sum of indexed-copy cycles has unique cycle coordinates
exclusions.reason: Cycle directness is explicitly algebraic and only concerns finite-support tuples and chains.

evidence.quote: Here and below a spectral subset is *separated* if its distance from the rest of the spectrum is positive. Its indicator is continuous on the spectrum. The spectral projection therefore belongs to the unital $C^*$-algebra containing the operator, by continuous functional calculus.

outputs.exact_statement: There exist a finitely generated torsion-free discrete group $G_{\mathrm{proj}}$ and a projection $e\in C_r^*(G_{\mathrm{proj}})$ such that $$0<\tau_{G_{\mathrm{proj}}}(e)<\frac12.$$ In particular, $e$ is neither zero nor the identity.

If $\Lambda$ is a subgroup of a discrete group $K$, the inclusion of group algebras extends to an isometric unital inclusion $C_r^*(\Lambda)\subseteq C_r^*(K)$, preserving the canonical traces and their finite matrix extensions.

Let $\Lambda$ be a discrete group and $p\in M_N(C_r^*(\Lambda))$ a projection with $$02. Set $$U=(\lambda_K(t_1),\ldots,\lambda_K(t_N)),\qquad A=pU^*Up.$$ Then $A$ is invertible in the unital corner $pM_N(C_r^*(K))p$, and $$e=(Up)A^{-1}(Up)^* \label{scalar:projection-formula}$$ is a projection in the scalar algebra $C_r^*(K)$ with $\tau_K(e)=a$. If $\Lambda$ is finitely generated and torsion-free, then so is $K$.

There exist a finitely generated torsion-free discrete group $\Gamma_{\mathrm{proj}}$, a finite integer $N\ge1$, and a self-adjoint element $T\in M_N(\mathbb C[\Gamma_{\mathrm{proj}}])$, in its regular representation, with a nonempty separated spectral subset whose spectral projection $p_0$ satisfies $$p_0\in M_N(C_r^*(\Gamma_{\mathrm{proj}})),\qquad
 0<\tau_{\Gamma_{\mathrm{proj}},N}(p_0)<\frac12.$$

The injections and spills can be chosen so that the following holds for every family, separately on each side. Let $\mathcal I$ be the set of slots for its one adjacent pair, let $n_{\rm sl}=|\mathcal
I|$, and let $$M_a:\mathbb F _2^s\longrightarrow\mathbb F _2^{s+\alpha}
 \quad\hbox{or}\quad
 M_c:\mathbb F _2^s\longrightarrow\mathbb F _2^{s+\beta}$$ be diagonal multiplication followed by its spill. For every nonzero linear functional $\zeta$ on the output space, every value of the restricted input functional $\zeta M_a$, or $\zeta M_c$, occurs on at most $0.55n_{\rm sl}$ slots after restriction to any nonempty initial segment of the $s$ input bits. On all $s$ input bits, the corresponding bound is $10^{-3}n_{\rm sl}$.

Fix an actual pair $(i,k)$ and every table at its lower marked positions. The current last-block tables can be sampled so that the remaining random choices in its $Y^0$-block are independent uniform perfect matchings between pairs of clusters, each cluster having $2^t$ slot incidences. There is one matching for each tuple consisting of the family, serial number, $x$, and all preceding $u$-blocks on both sides. Every edge in each cluster pair is a possible edge, and its matching is used only for that pair of clusters.

Let $C$ denote conditioned data. Conditional on $C$, let $U\in\mathbb F_2^t$ and $V\in\mathbb F_2^m$ be independent uniform vectors, independent also of auxiliary data $W$. For $1\leq a\leq q$ let $M_a:\mathbb F_2^t\to\mathbb F_2^m$ be linear, let $o_a=o_a(C,W)$, and let $f_a(C,z)$ be complex functions that do not depend separately on $U,V,W$. Set $$F=\frac1q\sum_a f_a(C,V+M_aU+o_a),\qquad \mu(C)=\frac1q\sum_a2^{-m}\sum_z f_a(C,z).$$ Suppose that for every nonzero linear functional $\zeta:\mathbb F_2^m\to\mathbb F_2$, every class of indices on which $\zeta M_a$ is the same has size at most $\theta q$. Then $$\begin{aligned} \mathbb E(F\mid C,W,U)&=\mu(C),\label{exp:conditional-mean}\\ \mathbb E|F-\mathbb E(F\mid C)|^2 &\leq\theta\,\mathbb E\left[ \frac1q\sum_a2^{-m}\sum_z|f_a(C,z)|^2\right]. \label{exp:conditional-variance} \end{aligned}$$ The conclusion applies with $\theta=10^{-3}$ for a full active $s$-block and with $\theta=0.55$ for any nonempty active initial part, using the coefficient multiplicity bounds of Lemma 5.

For every height pair, and every fixed choice of its lower-cutoff tables, the mean incidence $M$ satisfies $$\big\|M:\mathbf1_B^\perp\longrightarrow
                   \mathbf1_A^\perp\big\|
 \leq\sqrt{16\cdot10^{-3}+0.55}<0.8.$$ The bound is uniform in the number of full blocks, the final active length $1\leq t\leq s$, and $0\leq\alpha,\beta\leq2$.
With lower tables fixed, for every nonempty $Z$ of volume at most $E$, $$\mathbb P\{b(Z)<v(Z)/20\}\leq\exp(-v(Z)/400).$$

For all sufficiently large $\ell$, independently of the height pair and of its previously fixed lower tables, its current tables can be chosen so that [exp:actual-cut] holds. For this choice, the incidence operator of the actual $Y^0$ block, with each entry normalized by $\sqrt{dD'}$ in counting Hilbert spaces, sends normalized constants to normalized constants, as does its adjoint, and has norm at most $1-\chi$ between their orthogonal complements, where $$\chi=\frac1{800}.$$

Suppose two nonbacktracking paths in $Y^\#$ have the same oriented label word. At corresponding $A$-positions of radius at least $2j+1$, both padded streams agree through length $r+sj$, for every $j\geq0$. At corresponding $B$-positions of radius at least $2j$, both padded streams agree through length $sj$, for every $j\geq1$. The compared positions need not be in the same layer.

Fix a layer and a side. A nonempty cyclically reduced oriented label word is the word of at most one based cyclically nonbacktracking closed path with its base on that layer and side. Consequently the number of vertices of $A_i$, or of $B_i$, supporting such a closed path of length at most $g_i$ is at most $$\sum_{a=1}^{\lfloor g_i\rfloor}(2m_\ell)^a.$$ For all sufficiently large $\ell$, this is a fraction at most $2^{-0.9H_i}$ of either vertex set, uniformly in $i$.

For all sufficiently large $\ell$, the preceding choices give a graph $Y^0$ on sets of sizes $|A_i|=d2^{H_i}$ and $|B_i|=2^{H_i}$, and its induced subgraph $Y$, with these properties.* 1. *For every $|i-k|\leq1$, the $Y^0$-block between $A_i$ and $B_k$ has degrees $d,D_{ik}$ with $D_{ik}=D2^{|i|-|k|}$. Its counting incidence divided by $\sqrt{dD_{ik}}$ maps normalized constants to normalized constants, as does its adjoint. On their orthogonal complements its norm is at most $1-\chi$, with the absolute constant $\chi$ of Proposition 10.* 2. *The fraction removed from any $A_i$ or $B_i$ is at most $\varepsilon_\ell$ of [prune:total-budget].* 3. *The labels of $Y$ are folded, with positive alphabet size at most $m_\ell=O(d2^r(1+s)^2)$.* 4. *Every nonbacktracking path in $Y$ beginning at layer $i$ and having length at least $L_i$ is determined by its oriented word among all paths in $Y$, including paths beginning in other layers.* 5. *There is no nonempty cyclically nonbacktracking closed path in $Y$, based at layer $i$, of length at most $g_i$.

Let $\Pi$ be the orthogonal projection that retains the vertices of $Y$ in the counting Hilbert space of the full tower, with any additional Hilbert-space tensor factor. Let $C$ be the subspace of vectors that are constant on each separate $A_i$ and $B_i$ in the vertex coordinate. Then $$\|(1-\Pi)|_C\|\leq\sqrt{\varepsilon_\ell}.$$ In particular the same bound holds on every subspace of $C$, uniformly in the additional tensor factor.

There are absolute constants $C_*,C_\bullet$ such that, for sufficiently large $\ell$, the preceding hypotheses have the following consequences. Every component map $\phi:C\to X$ is an embedding. Index copies by pairs $(C,\phi)$ modulo the equivalence $$(C,\phi)\sim
 (\delta_a C,\phi\delta_a^{-1}),\qquad a\in F.$$ Thus an indexed copy $Q$ remembers its source component and source vertices up to this deck alignment, in addition to its embedded image. There is a well-order of these copies and an induced intrinsic ball $B(Q)$ in each $Q$ such that*

1.  *every vertex of $Q$ shared with an earlier copy belongs to $B(Q)$;*

2.  *the subgraph of $Q$ consisting of all edges with at least one endpoint in $B(Q)$ is a forest;*

3.  *for every vertex of $B(Q)$ lying over layer $i$, $$|V(B(Q))|\le\mathfrak w_i,
     \qquad \mathfrak w_i=2^{C_\bullet H_i};
     \label{geo:weight}$$*

4.  *if $D_Q$ is $V(Q)$ minus its vertices shared with earlier copies, the domains $D_Q$ are pairwise disjoint, and deleting every edge of $Q$ whose two endpoints lie in $D_Q$, for all $Q$, leaves a forest in $X$.*

*Furthermore $\Gamma_{\mathrm{proj}}$ is torsion-free. None of the constants depends on $F$, the voltage values, the number of components of $P$, or $|S|$.

In either minimum diagram the following statements hold.*

1.  *No bounded face has a freely trivial label word.*

2.  *No edge separating two distinct bounded faces has aligned source incidences. Nor does an edge between a bounded face and an adjustable exterior side have aligned source incidences.*

3.  *There is no unmarked vertex of degree one, and no bridge having both incidences on a bounded face.*

*Here alignment means that, when both incidences are read in the same direction, a left deck transformation identifies their source edges.

Every arc incident with a bounded face has length less than $L_i$, when read from an endpoint in layer $i$ on that face. Its length is also less than $L_i$ on any adjustable-side incidence with which it is compared. Every bounded face has at least twenty arc incidences. If $b$ is the number of arcs and there are at most $m$ marked vertices, then $$b\le 3J+3m-3,\qquad 20J\le 2b,\qquad b\le 6m.
 \label{geo:euler}$$ These statements require only $C_*\ge10^4$ and sufficiently large $\ell$.
All component label maps $C\to X$ are injective on vertices and formal edges. The indexed copies of Theorem 15 are therefore defined.
In $\widehat X$ the integral oriented chain of any edge loop of length $n$ is a sum of at most $12n$ oriented chains of edge loops of length at most four.

Let a connected graph with unit edge lengths have the conclusion of Lemma 19. Every geodesic triangle on its vertices is $D_0$-thin, where one may take $D_0=10^6$. Thinness here measures distance to the vertices on the other two sides.

Fix a positive integer $L$. For sufficiently large $\ell$, uniformly in $Q$ and $i$, if a path in $\widehat X$ of length at most $L$ joins $u,x\in Q$, with $u$ in layer $i$, and avoids $c_Q$, then $$d_Q(u,x)\le24(L+1)L_i.
 \label{geo:avoidance-bound}$$ Here the threshold for $\ell$ can depend on $L$, which will subsequently be an absolute constant.
There is a well-order of the indexed copies for which the first three assertions of Theorem 15 hold.

For every field $k$, inclusion of the indexed copies induces an isomorphism of vector spaces $$\bigoplus_Q Z_1(Q;k)\ \longrightarrow\ Z_1(X;k),
 \qquad (c_Q)_Q\longmapsto\sum_Q c_Q.
 \label{geo:cycle-decomposition}$$ The direct sum is algebraic, so every tuple used has finite support.

Put $$D_Q=V(Q)\setminus\bigcup_{R<Q}V(R),\qquad
 E_{\mathrm{int}}=\bigcup_Q
 \{e\in E(Q):\text{ both endpoints of }e\text{ lie in }D_Q\}.$$ The $D_Q$ are pairwise disjoint, $V(Q)\setminus D_Q\subseteq V(B(Q))$, and the formal graph $(V(X),E(X)\setminus E_{\mathrm{int}})$ is a forest. Each edge in $E_{\mathrm{int}}$ belongs to the displayed set for exactly one $Q$.

Let $$\mathcal I=\{(Q,x):Q\text{ an indexed copy},\ x\in V(Q)\}.$$ There is a canonical bijection $$\mathcal I\longrightarrow\Gamma_{\mathrm{proj}}\times V(Y),\qquad
 (Q,x)\longmapsto(x,\operatorname{type}_Q(x)),
 \label{geo:incidence-bijection}$$ where the type is the base vertex under the unique source vertex of the embedding. It intertwines left translation of $\Gamma_{\mathrm{proj}}$ with left translation of the first coordinate, with the base type fixed. In particular, for a fixed $x\in\Gamma_{\mathrm{proj}}$ and $v\in V(Y)$ there is exactly one incidence at $x$ of type $v$, even when $P$ is disconnected.

The stabilizer in $\Gamma_{\mathrm{proj}}$ of an indexed copy embeds into the subgroup of $F$ preserving any representative source component. In particular that stabilizer has no nonidentity finite-order element.

For every field $k$, the augmented cellular chain complex $$0\longrightarrow C_2(Z;k)\xrightarrow{\partial_2}C_1(Z;k)
 \xrightarrow{\partial_1}C_0(Z;k)\xrightarrow{\varepsilon}k
 \longrightarrow0
 \label{geo:acyclic-complex}$$ is exact.
The finitely generated group $\Gamma_{\mathrm{proj}}$ in [geo:presentation] is torsion-free.

Let $S$ be a finite connected metric graph with positive edge lengths, total length at most $Cg$, and girth greater than $g>0$. Girth means the infimum of lengths of embedded circles, with value $+\infty$ for a tree. Put $$B(C)=\max\{1,\lceil20C\rceil\}^{\,2}.$$ Then $b_1(S)\le B(C)$. Vertices of degree one and parallel edges are allowed.

Let $W$ be a nonempty cyclically nonbacktracking closed walk in a unit-edge graph of girth greater than $g$, with length at most $Cg$. There is a spanning tree of its support such that, after its edge variables are set equal to the identity, the holonomy word has a nontrivial free reduction of length at most $$L(C)=\lceil3CB(C)\rceil.$$ If $m>L(C)$, that word is not an identity on the group $U_{\mathbb Z}$ of upper unitriangular $m$-by-$m$ integer matrices. Every entry of any word in generic upper unitriangular matrices and their inverses is a polynomial of total degree at most $m-1$ in their upper entries. Nonidentity is preserved if each edge variable is multiplied on either side by a fixed upper unitriangular matrix.

The laws above are polynomial with integer coefficients in $(\lambda,b-1,z)$. Give the coordinates weights $$\operatorname{wt}(b-1)_{ij}=j-i,\quad
 \operatorname{wt}\lambda_{ij}=m-(j-i),\quad
 \operatorname{wt}z=m.$$ Scaling weight $a$ by $y^a$ defines an automorphism $\Delta_y$, for $y>0$, and $c(\Delta_y\gamma,\Delta_y\eta)=y^m c(\gamma,\eta)$. Lebesgue coordinate measure is both left and right Haar measure on $E$ and $\bar E$; inversion preserves it. The Jacobian of $\Delta_y$ on $\bar E$ is $y^{mn_{\mathrm f}}$. The integer coordinate sets $E_{\mathbb Z}$ and $\bar E_{\mathbb Z}$ are countable nilpotent torsion-free groups.

Let $L$ be a countable group with a right action as above and let $I,J$ be finite or countable auxiliary sets. On $\mathcal H_I=\ell^2(L)\otimes\ell^2(I)$, define, for equivariant positive bounded $B$, $$\operatorname{Tr}_I(B)
   =\sum_{i\in I}\langle B\delta_{(1,i)},\delta_{(1,i)}\rangle
       \in[0,\infty].$$ For a bounded equivariant $A:\mathcal H_I\to\mathcal H_J$, $$\label{nil:adjoint-square}
 \operatorname{Tr}_I(A^*A)=\operatorname{Tr}_J(AA^*).$$ This trace is additive on positive operators, monotone, and faithful on projections, and does not depend on the chosen orthonormal basis of the auxiliary Hilbert space. Equivariantly equivalent projections have equal size. A bounded equivariant map injective on the range of a projection $P$, with image there contained in the range of $Q$, gives $\operatorname{Tr}(P)\le\operatorname{Tr}(Q)$. These statements apply to countable orthogonal sums and to each Fourier fiber. Integrating a fiber trace gives the identity trace before Fourier transformation.

For each sign $\epsilon$, there is a Schwartz function $J_\epsilon$ on $\bar E$ with $$J_\epsilon^{*_\epsilon}=J_\epsilon,\qquad
 J_\epsilon *_\epsilon J_\epsilon=J_\epsilon,\qquad
 \|J_\epsilon\|_{L^2(\bar E)}=1.$$

For positive integer weights $w_1,\ldots,w_k$, set $$\mathcal L_y=\prod_{a=1}^k y^{w_a}\mathbb Z,\qquad
 v_y=y^{w_1+\cdots+w_k},\qquad 0<y\le1.$$ For Schwartz $f$ on $\mathbb R^k$, $$v_y\sum_{a\in\mathcal L_y}f(a)\longrightarrow
                   \int_{\mathbb R^k}f(x)\,dx.$$ The corresponding normalized sums of absolute values are uniformly bounded. For jointly Schwartz $G(a,h)$ on $\mathbb R^k\times\mathbb R^k$, and every $M$, $$\label{nil:riemann-weighted}
 \sup_h(1+|h|)^M
 \left|v_y\sum_{a\in\mathcal L_y}G(a,h)
                    -\int G(a,h)\,da\right|\le C_{G,M}y.$$

The functions $J_\epsilon$ in Equation [nil:K] may be replaced by smooth compactly supported $J_\epsilon^\flat$ at arbitrarily small uniform coefficient $\ell^1$ cost for sufficiently small $|\theta|$. For fixed such a function, replacing $\alpha>0$ by $\beta>0$, where $|\log(\alpha/\beta)|\le a\le1$, changes the coefficients $$\alpha^{n_{\mathrm f}} J_\epsilon^\flat(\Delta_{\alpha^{1/m}}\gamma)$$ by $\ell^1$ amount at most $Ca$, uniformly for sufficiently small $\alpha,\beta$. These coefficient bounds imply operator bounds when evaluated using any family of unitaries.

On the second quotient factor, define $$V_t(\gamma)=u_t(\gamma)\otimes R_\gamma.$$ Its multiplier is $\mathrm e((t-\delta)c)$, and it is unitarily equivalent to $N$ copies of $u_{t-\delta}$. The equivalence fixes the quotient-identity fiber, preserving the identity trace with its unnormalized matrix sum. Thus every coefficient sum, and every continuous spectral function of it, has the same operator norm as its evaluation in $u_{t-\delta}$; the identity trace of a projection is multiplied by $N$.

There is a smooth nonnegative $h$, supported in $(-1,1)$ and positive on $[-0.7,0.7]$, with $\sum_{i\in\mathbb Z}h(v-i)^2=1$ for every $v\in\mathbb R$. For $0<t<\delta$, set $$\label{nil:h}
 b(t)=\kappa^{-1}\log_2\frac{t}{\delta-t},\qquad
 h_i(t)=h(b(t)-i),$$ and extend $h_i$ by zero to the rest of the circle. Each extension is smooth. The active set $J(t)=\{i:h_i(t)\ne0\}$ has one or two elements, adjacent if two, and $\sum_i h_i(t)^2=1$ on the open interval. With $w_i=q^{-1}2^{-\kappa|i|}$, its support length and derivatives satisfy $$|\operatorname{supp}h_i|\le C_\kappa w_i,\qquad
 \|\partial_t^j h_i\|_\infty\le C_{\kappa,j}w_i^{-j}.$$ On an active index $i$, uniformly in $\ell,i,t$, $$\begin{aligned}
 \log_2(t^{-1})
 &=\log_2q+\kappa\max(-i,0)+O_\kappa(1),\label{nil:log-t}\\
 \log_2((\delta-t)^{-1})
 &=\log_2q+\kappa\max(i,0)+O_\kappa(1),\label{nil:log-tau}\\
 t(\delta-t)&\le 2^\kappa q^{-2}2^{-\kappa|i|}.
                                                  \label{nil:product}
\end{aligned}$$

For $0<t<\delta$, define an isometry on $p(t)\mathcal H_t$ by $$V_*(t)\zeta=2^{-1/2}
 \left(\bigoplus_i h_i(t)a_i\otimes\zeta\right)
 \oplus
 2^{-1/2}\left(\bigoplus_i h_i(t)b_i\otimes\zeta\right),
 \qquad E_*(t)=V_*(t)V_*(t)^*.
 \label{spec:model-isometry}$$ Then $O(t)E_*(t)=E_*(t)$, $\|O(t)\|\leq1$, and $$O(t)|_{(1-E_*(t))\mathcal H^0_t}\leq(1-\chi)I,
 \qquad
 \operatorname{tr}_{\mathrm{id}}E_*(t)
       =\operatorname{tr}_{\mathrm{id}}p(t).
 \label{spec:model-gap-trace}$$ Set $E_*(t)=0$ outside the window; the same upper bound holds there. Furthermore $$\|(1-\Pi)E_*(t)\|\leq\sqrt{\beta_\ell}
 \label{spec:model-cut}$$ uniformly in $t$.

For every fixed $\eta>0$, and for all sufficiently large $\ell$, there are voltages $z_e\in F$ and matrices $W_e\in M_N(\mathbb C)$ on the positively oriented edges of $Y$ with the following properties.*

1.  *There is a constant $C_\eta$, independent of $\ell$ and the layer, such that $\|W_e\|\le C_\eta$. Augmenting an original tower label by its matrix weight gives a finite positive alphabet of size $o(dD)$. The normalizing number $D_{ik}$ is determined by the original part of the label.*

2.  *The voltage cover has no nonempty cyclically nonbacktracking closed walk based in layer $i$ of length at most $C_*H_i/\log_2d$.*


3.  *Let $T_P$, extended by zero on the deleted vertex indices, have entries from $B_k$ to $A_i$ $$\label{sam:entries}
     (T_P)_{ab}=
     \frac1{\sqrt{dD_{ik}}}\sum_{e:a\to b}W_e\rho(z_e),
     \qquad a\in A_i,\quad b\in B_k,$$ with the adjoint entries in the opposite direction. Then $$\label{sam:approx}
     \|T_P-\Pi O\Pi\|\le\eta.$$ Both operators have layer width one. In particular, their central Fourier fields satisfy the same inequality almost everywhere, including $\|T_P(t)\|\le\eta$ outside the open window.*

*The matrices $W_e$ are the actual weights of the individual edges of the voltage cover, so $T_P$ reduces on each component of that cover.

Set $M=\lfloor d^{1/32}\rfloor$, with $q=d^{A_*}$ and $A_*$ fixed. Consider at most $C(1+\log q)$ finite distributions of operators $W\rho(g)$ on $\ell^2(F)\otimes\mathbb C^N$. Suppose $\|W\|\le B_0$, every possible group coordinate is bounded by $q^a$, and $N\le q^a$, for fixed constants $a,B_0,C$. For each fixed $\varepsilon>0$, and sufficiently large $\ell$, each expectation has an $M$-term empirical average within $\varepsilon$ in the full regular norm. The averages may be chosen for all the distributions simultaneously.

Let a finite graph have maximum degree $\Delta\ge1$. Fix a vertex $v$ and an integer $l\ge1$. Suppose the support of every closed walk under consideration has first Betti number at most $b$. The number of length-$2l$ closed walks from $v$ in which no undirected edge occurs exactly once is at most $$C_b^l\Delta^l.$$ Multiple edges, if present, are treated as distinct edges.

Let $A=A^*$ on a Hilbert space, with $\|A\|\leq2$, and let $E$ be a reducing projection such that $$\|(A-I)E\|\leq a,\qquad A|_{(1-E)\mathcal H}\leq(1-b)I,\qquad 032, $E$ and $E^J$ have equal identity traces. These statements include $E=0$.

Suppose $B=B^*$ has a reducing projection $F$ with $BF=F$, and its complementary spectrum is contained in $[-2,1-b]$, where $0<b<1$. Let $r_0>0$ satisfy $r_0\leq b/2$ and $r_0<1$. If $A=A^*$ and $\|A-B\|\leq u<r_0$, the circle $\mathcal C_{r_0}=\{z:|z-1|=r_0\}$ lies in the resolvent sets of both operators. The enclosed spectral projection $F_A$ satisfies $$\|F_A-F\|\leq\frac{u}{r_0-u}.
 \label{spec:projection-distance}$$ Its enclosed spectrum lies in $[1-u,1+u]$; all the other spectrum of $A$ is at most $1-b+u$. If $u<r_0/2$, the projections $F_A$ and $F$ are equivalent by a partial isometry belonging to the algebra of bounded operators generated by them. This equivalence preserves any common equivariance and its identity trace.

The operator $T_P$ has a separated upper spectral projection $E_P$, obtained by integration around $\mathcal C_{r_0}$. It satisfies $$\|T_P\|\leq2,\qquad
 \|(T_P-I)E_P\|\leq\alpha,\qquad
 T_P|_{(1-E_P)\mathcal H}\leq(1-\chi+\alpha)I.
 \label{spec:cover-gap}$$ In the central direct integral, for almost every $t$, $$\operatorname{tr}_{\mathrm{id}}E_P(t)
  =\begin{cases}
        \operatorname{tr}_{\mathrm{id}}p(t),&0<t<\delta,\\
        0,&t\notin(0,\delta).
    \end{cases}
 \label{spec:exact-fiber-trace}$$ The projection $E_P$ is nonzero and reduces to the connected components of $P$. Its diagonal at a lifted vertex depends only on the base vertex.

For the fixed choice of $\eta$ in Equation [spec:eta-choice], $$\mathcal S\leq96\mu_\ell=o(1). \label{spec:S-small}$$ In particular the bound contains no additional factor equal to a layer cardinality or to the matrix dimension already included in $\mu_\ell$.

Let $D_Q$ and $B(Q)$ be the assigned domain and trimming ball from Theorem 15. Then $$\|\mathbf1_{B(Q)}E_Q\|^2\leq\mathcal S. \label{spec:ball-HS}$$ For $\mathcal S\leq1/4$, the compression of $T_Q$ to $\ell^2(D_Q)\otimes\mathbb C^N$ is within $\alpha+20\sqrt{\mathcal S}$ of an operator $C_Q$ which is $1$ on a projection $F_Q$ equivalent to $E_Q$, has norm at most $2$, and is at most $1-\chi+\alpha$ on the complementary space. In particular $F_Q\ne0$ whenever $E_Q\ne0$.
Suppose a countable forest has maximum degree at most $m_1$, and a self-adjoint adjacency on it has matrix edge weights of norms at most $w_1$. Its norm is at most $2w_1\sqrt{m_1}$.

For sufficiently large $\ell$, the operator in Equation [spec:Cayley-operator] satisfies $$\operatorname{spec}T \subset(-\infty,1-\chi+4\alpha]\, \cup[1-3\alpha,1+3\alpha]. \label{spec:global-spectrum}$$ The second spectral part is nonempty. Its projection $$p_0=\mathbf1_{[1-\chi/4,\infty)}(T) \in M_N(C_r^*(\Gamma_{\mathrm{proj}})) \label{spec:p0}$$ is consequently nonzero.

Put $I_Q=V(Q)\setminus D_Q\subset B(Q)$. For every $\xi\in\mathcal H$, $$\sum_Q\|E_Q(\xi|_{I_Q})\|^2\leq\mathcal S\|\xi\|^2,
 \label{spec:all-copy-cut-loss}$$ where restrictions are extended by zero inside their copies.

The formula $$A\xi=\big(E_Q(\xi|_{V(Q)})\big)_Q
       \quad(\xi\in\mathcal H)
 \label{spec:analysis-operator}$$ defines a bounded equivariant operator $A:\mathcal H\to\mathcal U$, with $\|A\|\leq1+\sqrt{\mathcal S}$. Its kernel $K$ is a closed invariant subspace, and every $\xi\in K$ satisfies $$E_Q(\xi|_{V(Q)})=0\quad\text{for every indexed }Q.
 \label{spec:kernel-restrictions}$$ Moreover, $$\operatorname{Tr}_{\Gamma_{\mathrm{proj}}} P_{K^\perp}\leq\mathcal S_0.
 \label{spec:kernel-complement-size}$$

With the choices in Equations [spec:S-final-choice] and [spec:forest-error], $$\langle T\xi,\xi\rangle \leq(1-\chi+3\alpha)\|\xi\|^2 \quad(\xi\in K). \label{spec:kernel-form-bound}$$ Consequently the bounded equivariant map $P_{K^\perp}:p_0\mathcal H\to K^\perp$ is injective, and $$0<\tau_{\Gamma_{\mathrm{proj}},N}(p_0) \leq\mathcal S_0\leq\mathcal S<1/2. \label{spec:strict-trace}$$

For the fixed choices made above and some sufficiently large integer $\ell$, the construction defines a finitely generated torsion-free group $\Gamma_{\mathrm{proj}}$, a positive integer $N$, and the self-adjoint finite group-algebra matrix $T$ in Equation [spec:Cayley-operator]. Its spectrum in the reduced representation has the separation in Equation [spec:global-spectrum]. The resulting projection $p_0$ in Equation [spec:p0] belongs to $M_N(C_r^*(\Gamma_{\mathrm{proj}}))$ and obeys $$0<\sum_{j=1}^N\tau_{\Gamma_{\mathrm{proj}}}((p_0)_{jj})<\frac12.$$
